summary: Oisterwijk is not a free-parking town: the municipal Verordening parkeerbelastingen 2026 (in force from 1 January 2026) charges for parking in a centre zone (De Lind, Dorpsstraat, Hoogstraat, Kerkstraat, Stationsstraat, Burgemeester Verwielstraat) at 0.25 euro for the first quarter-hour and 2.40 euro per hour from the second hour, and in an 'other' zone of streets and car parks at 1.55 euro per hour with a day ticket of 6.20 euro. Paid hours are Monday-Thursday 09:00-18:00, Friday 09:00-21:00 and Saturday 09:00-17:00, with free parking in the evening and on Sundays. Because paid parking pushed long-stay parkers into residential streets around the centre, the council made some edge-of-centre car parks free and introduced two-hour disc zones (Peperstraat, Schoolstraat in 2021) to manage the overspill (2021 position). Public charging is being expanded (11 new charge points in an October 2026 traffic decision) and a Vattenfall pilot from August 2026 tests chargers without reserved bays. A 2022 recreation and tourism study estimated about 416,000 visits a year to the Oisterwijkse Bossen en Vennen and flagged peak-time parking in verges as an issue to analyse. The designation map shows eight paid car parks, including Stationsplein and Spoorlaan-Jumbo near the station, all at 1.55 euro per hour. The municipal website was offline when read on 21 October 2026, so no official page on the station park-and-ride, car park capacities or utilisation could be read.

items.text: On 11 December 2025 the council adopted the Verordening parkeerbelastingen 2026, applying from 1 January 2026: Zone Centrum costs 0.25 euro for the first quarter-hour, 0.55 euro per quarter for the second and third, 0.80 euro for the fourth, then 2.40 euro per hour from the second hour. Zone Overig (streets and car parks marked yellow on the designation map) costs 1.55 euro per hour, with a day ticket of 6.20 euro.
items.source_title: Verordening op de heffing en de invordering van parkeerbelastingen 2026 (Gemeenteblad 2025 nr. 561707)

items.text: The college's Aanwijzingsbesluit betaald parkeren Oisterwijk 2026 (signed 16 December 2025, in force 1 January 2026) sets paid-parking hours of Monday-Thursday 09:00-18:00, Friday 09:00-21:00 and Saturday 09:00-17:00; outside these hours and on Sundays parking is free. Payment is by coin, contactless card or by registering by phone/internet with the central system.

Residents' permit fees for 2026 are 49.65 euro for a first permit without private parking space and 114.00 euro with one; a second permit costs 114.00 or 226.75 euro. Business permits cost 152.70 euro (first, no private space) up to 609.60 euro (second, with private space). The fine (naheffingsaanslag) is 76.00 euro and no remission is granted.
items.source_title: Verordening op de heffing en de invordering van parkeerbelastingen 2026 (Gemeenteblad 2025 nr. 561707)

items.text: The 2026 ordinance exempts holders of a disabled parking card on marked disabled bays and electric vehicles that are actually charging at charge points from paid parking.
items.source_title: Verordening op de heffing en de invordering van parkeerbelastingen 2026 (Gemeenteblad 2025 nr. 561707)

items.text: Tariff history from the ordinances: for 2023 the centre rate from the second hour was 2.30 euro, the other zone 1.50 euro per hour and the day ticket 6.00 euro; the 2024 ordinance raised these to 2.40, 1.55 and 6.20 euro, and the 2025 and 2026 ordinances kept the same parking rates (only permit fees changed, e.g. first residents' permit 48.35 euro in 2025, 49.65 euro in 2026).

The attached map of the 2026 designation decision shows eight signed paid car parks, all in the 'other' zone at 1.55 euro per hour (day ticket 6.20 euro): Stationsplein, Gemullehoekenweg (two lots), Spoorlaan-Jumbo, Marktpad, Burg. Verwielstraat, Vloeiweg-AH and Vloeiweg-Mevio. The Spoorlaan street section along the station is also marked in the 'other' zone; the map does not name any park-and-ride lot or give space counts.
items.source_title: Bijlage I, kaart bij Aanwijzingsbesluit betaald parkeren Oisterwijk 2026 (read from the published image)

items.text: For comparison, the map attached to the 2019 designation decision showed the same eight car park numbers (including Stationsplein and Spoorlaan-Jumbo) with older rates: 0.20 euro first quarter-hour, 2.00 euro per hour from the second hour in the centre, 1.20 euro per hour elsewhere and a day ticket of 4.80 euro, i.e. the centre hourly rate has risen by 20 percent since 2019.
items.source_title: Bijlage I, kaart bij aanwijzingsbesluit betaald parkeren Oisterwijk 2019 (Overheid repository)

items.text: Policy rules of 2018 for the 'centrumschil' parking disc zone state that long-stay parkers cause nuisance in streets around the paid centre; residents and businesses inside the disc zone can apply for a licence-plate-linked exemption without time limit, granted per calendar year. The register shows these rules as in force on the page read on 21 October 2026.

On 4 September 2025 the college published a decision setting a 30-minute parking disc zone (Monday-Saturday 09:00-18:00) on four of 22 angled bays on the Moergestelseweg parallel road near the Tilburgseweg roundabout, because bays near local businesses were occupied all day and short-stay visitors found no space.
items.source_title: Het instellen van een parkeerschijfzone aan de Moergestelseweg in Oisterwijk (Gemeenteblad 2025 nr. 373477)

items.text: The council's Nota Parkeernormen (adopted 24 August 2016, replacing the 2010 Parkeerfondsverordening) sets parking standards for new developments by area (centre, edge zone, rest of built-up area) and a mobility fund: a developer who cannot provide required spaces on site pays 5,000 euro per space in the centre (7,500 euro if no compensation space is possible) and 3,500 or 5,000 euro elsewhere (2016 price level, indexed yearly). This is an old policy document; a newer one was not found.

In a decision published on 5 March 2021 the college introduced a two-hour parking disc zone in the Schoolstraat (Monday-Thursday 09:00-18:00, Friday 09:00-21:00, Saturday 09:00-17:00), joining an existing disc zone in the Peperstraat. It stated that paid parking in the centre pushes long-stay parkers into surrounding residential streets, that some edge-of-centre car parks had been made free but a parking survey showed this was not enough, and that a free car park at the Peperstraat remained available for long-stay parkers (as of 2021).
items.source_title: Het invoeren van een parkeerschijfzone in de Schoolstraat te Oisterwijk (Staatscourant 2021, 11744)

items.text: A 2022 study for the municipality, citing the Koopstromenonderzoek 2021, shows visitors rated parking by car in Oisterwijk centre 7.0 out of 10, below Moergestel and Haaren (both 8.1) and below the centre's overall score of 8.2.
items.source_title: Bouwstenen beleid recreatie en toerisme Oisterwijk (Stedelijke Planning, 18 July 2022)

items.text: The same 2022 study estimates the Oisterwijkse Bossen en Vennen draw about 416,000 visits a year (fifth most visited nature area in Noord-Brabant) and recommends analysing peak-time bottlenecks such as parking in verges and adding parking places, and possibly an extra Natuurpoort location; these are recommendations, not decisions.
items.source_title: Bouwstenen beleid recreatie en toerisme Oisterwijk (Stedelijke Planning, 18 July 2022)

items.text: On 29 September 2026 Omroep Brabant reported that the municipality is extending its public charging network, with two bays assigned to each new charge point (only for vehicles connected to charge), placed via traffic decisions with a six-week objection period. Locations were chosen on traffic safety, pedestrian space, green and grid connection.
items.source_title: Nieuwe openbare laadpalen in Oisterwijk en omgeving (Omroep Brabant, 29 Sep 2026)

items.text: The municipality and Vattenfall run a pilot from 1 August 2026 to 31 January 2027 at six locations (Donatus Haaren, Kruizenmunt, Van Beugenkwartier, Hopveld Moergestel, Drogerij and Den Deel) where chargers have no reserved bays and any car may park. The 7 July 2026 article by the same broadcaster lists a slightly different location set (including Langeweg, Langvennen Noord, Moergestelseweg) and also gives July 2027 as the end of the pilot besides 31 January 2027, so details differ between the articles.

On 1 October 2026 the college published a traffic decision (dated 22 September 2026) reserving two bays at each of 11 new charge points, mostly where existing chargers are heavily used plus one strategic site (Sportlaan 22). Chargers come under the provinces' July 2024 concession with Vattenfall InCharge; the decision states a possible rise in parking pressure is no reason to refrain from placing chargers.

gaps: https://www.oisterwijk.nl/parkeren and https://www.oisterwijk.nl/betaald-parkeren: the municipal website showed a 'Website offline' maintenance notice when read on 21 October 2026, so no official page on parking zones, car park lists, P+R or station parking could be read.

Capacities (number of spaces) of the centre car parks are not given in any source read; the P+R Spoorlaan lot is not named as such on the 2026 designation map, so it could not be matched to a numbered car park.
No source found or opened on the P+R at Spoorlaan/Oisterwijk station (capacity, tariff, operator, NS/ProRail plans).

No mobility vision, current parking policy note or council papers (raadsinformatie) were readable (the council information site returned no content); no decisions on new car parks, closures or tariff changes were found beyond the annual ordinances; the current status of the free Peperstraat car park (2021 mention) was not confirmed.
No source opened on utilisation statements for centre car parks; no official source opened on parking at Oisterwijkse Bossen en Vennen (Natuurpoort, Van Tienhovenlaan) beyond the 2022 study.
